The `terms.tsx` header does not include a visible language-code hint for the two contract versions being fetched — small UX nit, current shows 'Versione v1' only after loading, which is fine.
seed_data_creation: One ephemeral anonymous user was created per test module (auto-deleted in fixture teardown).
context_for_next_testing_agent: The frontend UI test in browser used a hand-injected JWT into localStorage. Note that the app's storage layer JSON-parses stored values, so any manual token injection must use JSON.stringify(token) — using the raw JWT triggers 'storage retrieve(parse error)' warnings and leaves AuthContext unauthenticated, which means api.acceptLegalBoth() will silently no-op. When you need an end-to-end UI acceptance flow, either (a) drive login through the real /auth screen or (b) inject JSON.stringify(token) under localStorage key 'faide_token'.
rca_of_issue: No new bugs — both requested fixes verified working. The pool of 126 unique surnames + de-dup on 'Parisi' + global rotation yields 100 unique surnames and display_names across the entire bot cohort (previously ~39 unique). The `terms_accepted` boolean on /auth/me correctly requires BOTH versions matching TERMS_VERSION and NDA_VERSION.
